jelet-2025-q001.conceptSummary: Factor the quartic into two quadratics; every root then has modulus $1$.

steps.title: Roots of the first factor
steps.bodyLatex: $Z^{2} + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow Z = \pm i$, so $|Z| = 1$.

steps.title: Roots of the second factor
steps.bodyLatex: $Z^{2} - Z + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow Z = \dfrac{1 \pm i\sqrt{3}}{2}$, so $|Z| = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}} = 1$. (Equivalently, the product of the two conjugate roots is $1 = |Z|^{2}$.)

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: All four roots lie on the unit circle, so $|Z| = 1$. Answer: (D) $1$.

verification.note: SymPy: factor(Z^4 - Z^3 + 2Z^2 - Z + 1) = (Z^2+1)(Z^2-Z+1); all four roots have |Z| = 1.

jelet-2025-q002.conceptSummary: $A$ is the scalar matrix $\omega I$, so $A^{n} = \omega^{n} I$ and $\omega^{3} = 1$.

steps.title: Write $A$ as a scalar matrix
steps.bodyLatex: $A = \begin{bmatrix} \omega & 0 \\ 0 & \omega \end{bmatrix} = \omega I$, hence $A^{n} = \omega^{n} I$ for every positive integer $n$.

steps.title: Eliminate the other options
steps.bodyLatex:
$A = \omega I 
eq I$, $-A = -\omega I 
eq I$ and $A^{2} = \omega^{2} I 
eq I$ because $\omega 
eq 1$ and $\omega^{2} 
eq 1$. Answer: (C) $I$.

verification.note: SymPy: with w = exp(2*pi*i/3), (w*I_2)^2025 simplifies to I_2 and differs from A, -A, A^2.

jelet-2025-q003.conceptSummary: Use $(XY)^{T} = Y^{T}X^{T}$ together with $A^{T} = A$, $B^{T} = B$.

steps.title: Use symmetry
steps.bodyLatex: Since $A^{T} = A$ and $B^{T} = B$: $(AB - BA)^{T} = BA - AB = -(AB - BA)$.

steps.title: Classify
steps.bodyLatex: A matrix $X$ with $X^{T} = -X$ is skew symmetric. (It is not null in general, e.g. $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, $B = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ give $AB - BA = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.)

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) Skew symmetric matrix.

verification.note: SymPy: for generic symbolic symmetric 3x3 A, B, (AB-BA)^T + (AB-BA) = 0 while AB-BA is not identically zero.

jelet-2025-q004.conceptSummary: A $2 \times 2$ system has no solution when the coefficient determinant is $0$ and the equations are inconsistent.

steps.title: Coefficient determinant
steps.bodyLatex: $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} K+1 & 8 \\ K & K+3 \end{vmatrix} = (K+1)(K+3) - 8K = K^{2} - 4K + 3 = (K-1)(K-3)$.

steps.title: Candidates
steps.bodyLatex: $\Delta = 0 \Rightarrow K = 1$ or $K = 3$. For any other $K$ the system has a unique solution.

steps.title: Test $K = 1$
steps.bodyLatex: Equations: $2x + 8y = 4$ and $x + 4y = 2$. The first is twice the second, so the system is consistent with infinitely many solutions.

steps.title: Test $K = 3$
steps.bodyLatex: Equations: $4x + 8y = 12 \Rightarrow x + 2y = 3$ and $3x + 6y = 8 \Rightarrow x + 2y = \dfrac{8}{3}$. These are parallel distinct lines, so there is no solution.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Exactly one value ($K = 3$) gives no solution. Answer: (B) $1$.

verification.note: SymPy: det = (K-1)(K-3); rank test shows K=1 consistent, K=3 inconsistent -> exactly 1 value.

jelet-2025-q005.conceptSummary: $\tan u$ is homogeneous of degree $6$; apply Euler's theorem to $\tan u$.

steps.title: Identify the homogeneous function
steps.bodyLatex: Let $z = \tan u = \dfrac{x^{7} + y^{7}}{x}$. Replacing $(x, y)$ by $(tx, ty)$ gives $t^{6}z$, so $z$ is homogeneous of degree $n = 6$.

steps.title: Euler's theorem
steps.bodyLatex: $x\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} + y\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = 6z = 6\tan u$.

steps.title: Chain rule
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = \sec^{2}u\,\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}$ and $\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \sec^{2}u\,\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}$, so $\sec^{2}u\left(x\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x} + y\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right) = 6\tan u$.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.bodyLatex: $x\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x} + y\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y} = 6\tan u\cos^{2}u = 6\sin u\cos u = 3\sin 2u$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) $3\sin 2u$.

verification.note: SymPy: u = atan((x^7+y^7)/x); simplify(x*u_x + y*u_y - 3*sin(2u)) = 0.

jelet-2025-q006.conceptSummary: An odd integrand over a symmetric interval $[-a, a]$ integrates to $0$.

steps.title: Split numerator and denominator
steps.bodyLatex: Let $f(x) = \dfrac{x\left(|x| + \cos x + \sin^{2} x\right)}{\sec^{2} x + |x| + x^{4}}$. The bracket $|x| + \cos x + \sin^{2} x$ is even, and $x$ is odd, so the numerator is odd.

steps.title: Denominator
steps.bodyLatex: $\sec^{2} x$, $|x|$ and $x^{4}$ are all even, so the denominator is even and strictly positive ($\sec^{2} x \geq 1$).

steps.title: Parity of $f$
steps.bodyLatex: $f(-x) = \dfrac{-x\left(|x| + \cos x + \sin^{2} x\right)}{\sec^{2} x + |x| + x^{4}} = -f(x)$, so $f$ is odd and continuous on $[-1, 1]$.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.bodyLatex: $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)\,dx = 0$. Answer: (A) $0$.

verification.note: SymPy: f(-x) + f(x) simplifies to 0 (odd integrand); numerical quadrature on [-1,1] returns 0 to 1e-12.

steps.title: Simplify for $x \neq 3$
steps.bodyLatex: $f(x) = \dfrac{(x-3)(x-A)}{x-3} = x - A$ for $x \neq 3$.

steps.title: Impose continuity
steps.bodyLatex: $3 - A = f(3) = 5 \Rightarrow A = -2$. Answer: (D) $-2$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) $1$.

jelet-2025-q009.conceptSummary: Recognise $g(f + f')$ as the derivative of the product $fg$ when $g' = g$.

steps.title: Differentiate the product
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[f(x)g(x)\right] = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x)$.

steps.title: Use $g' = g$
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[f(x)g(x)\right] = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g(x) = g(x)\left[f(x) + f'(x)\right]$.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.bodyLatex: $\displaystyle\int g(x)\left[f(x) + f'(x)\right]dx = f(x)g(x) + C_{1}$.

steps.title: Note on option (D)
steps.bodyLatex: $f(x)g'(x)$ equals $f(x)g(x)$ only after substituting the hypothesis $g' = g$; options (A) and (B) differentiate to $f''g' + f'g''$ and $f''g + f'g'$, which are not the integrand. The direct antiderivative is $f(x)g(x) + C_{1}$. Answer: (C).

verification.note: SymPy: with g = c*e^x (general solution of g' = g), d/dx[f*g] - g*(f + f') = 0 for arbitrary f.

jelet-2025-q010.conceptSummary: Divide by $x^{4}$ (integrating factor) to make the equation exact; the result is $d\left(e^{x} + 2y^{2}/x^{2}\right) = 0$.

steps.title: Test exactness
steps.bodyLatex: $M = x^{4}e^{x} - 4xy^{2}$, $N = 4x^{2}y$: $\dfrac{\partial M}{\partial y} = -8xy$, $\dfrac{\partial N}{\partial x} = 8xy$, so the equation is not exact.

steps.title: Integrating factor
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{M_{y} - N_{x}}{N} = \dfrac{-16xy}{4x^{2}y} = -\dfrac{4}{x}$, a function of $x$ alone, so $\mu = e^{\int -4/x\,dx} = \dfrac{1}{x^{4}}$.

steps.title: Exact form
steps.bodyLatex: $\left(e^{x} - \dfrac{4y^{2}}{x^{3}}\right)dx + \dfrac{4y}{x^{2}}\,dy = 0$. Now $\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(e^{x} - \dfrac{4y^{2}}{x^{3}}\right) = -\dfrac{8y}{x^{3}} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\dfrac{4y}{x^{2}}\right)$.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.bodyLatex: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{4y}{x^{2}}\,dy = \dfrac{2y^{2}}{x^{2}}$ and $\displaystyle\int e^{x}\,dx = e^{x}$, so $e^{x} + \dfrac{2y^{2}}{x^{2}} = C$, i.e. $e^{x} + 2\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^{2} = C$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) $e^{x} + 2\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^{2} = C$.

verification.note: SymPy: F = e^x + 2y^2/x^2 satisfies F_x = M/x^4 and F_y = N/x^4; options A, C, D fail the same test.

steps.title: First term
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec{i} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{i}) = (\vec{i}\cdot\vec{i})\vec{a} - (\vec{i}\cdot\vec{a})\vec{i} = \vec{a} - a_{1}\vec{i}$, where $\vec{a} = a_{1}\vec{i} + a_{2}\vec{j} + a_{3}\vec{k}$.

steps.title: Second and third terms
steps.bodyLatex: Similarly $\vec{j} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{j}) = \vec{a} - a_{2}\vec{j}$ and $\vec{k} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{k}) = \vec{a} - a_{3}\vec{k}$.

steps.title: Add
steps.bodyLatex: Sum $= 3\vec{a} - (a_{1}\vec{i} + a_{2}\vec{j} + a_{3}\vec{k}) = 3\vec{a} - \vec{a} = 2\vec{a}$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $2\vec{a}$.

verification.note: SymPy: for symbolic a = (a1, a2, a3), sum of e x (a x e) over the standard basis equals 2a.

steps.title: Difference formula
steps.bodyLatex: $\tan^{-1}\alpha - \tan^{-1}\beta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\alpha - \beta}{1 + \alpha\beta}$ with $\alpha = x + k + 1$, $\beta = x + k$ gives $\dfrac{1}{1 + (x+k)(x+k+1)}$ (valid near $x = 0$, where $\alpha\beta > -1$).

steps.title: Telescope
steps.bodyLatex: $y = \displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\left[\tan^{-1}(x+k+1) - \tan^{-1}(x+k)\right] = \tan^{-1}(x+n) - \tan^{-1}x$.

verification.note: SymPy: 1+(x+k)(x+k+1) matches the three printed quadratics; direct differentiation of the n-term sum gives y'(0) = -n^2/(1+n^2) for n = 1..8.

jelet-2025-q013.conceptSummary: Classical probability over the $2^{4} = 16$ equally likely $0$–$1$ determinants.

steps.title: Sample space
steps.bodyLatex: $\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix}$ with $a, b, c, d \in \{0, 1\}$ gives $2^{4} = 16$ determinants.

steps.title: Probability
steps.bodyLatex: Favourable $= 3 + 3 = 6$, so $P = \dfrac{6}{16} = \dfrac{3}{8}$. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy/itertools: exhaustive enumeration of all 16 binary 2x2 matrices -> 6 non-zero determinants -> 3/8.

jelet-2025-q014.conceptSummary: Compare the distance between centres with $r_{1} + r_{2}$ and $|r_{1} - r_{2}|$.

steps.title: Classify
steps.bodyLatex: $C_{1}C_{2} = |r_{1} - r_{2}|$ means the circles touch internally, which allows exactly one common tangent (at the point of contact). Answer: (B) $1$.

verification.note: SymPy: centres (0,0),(3,4), radii 2,7; distance 5 = |7-2| -> internal tangency -> 1 common tangent.

jelet-2025-q015.conceptSummary: Total probability over the equally likely compositions of the urn before the white ball is added.

steps.title: Hypotheses
steps.bodyLatex: Before adding, the urn holds $0$, $1$ or $2$ white balls: $E_{0}, E_{1}, E_{2}$, each with probability $\dfrac{1}{3}$ (colours unknown, all compositions equally likely).

steps.title: After adding one white ball
steps.bodyLatex: The urn has $3$ balls with $1$, $2$ or $3$ white respectively, so $P(W \mid E_{0}) = \dfrac{1}{3}$, $P(W \mid E_{1}) = \dfrac{2}{3}$, $P(W \mid E_{2}) = 1$.

steps.title: Total probability
steps.bodyLatex: $P(W) = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} + 1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot 2 = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

steps.title: Cross-check
steps.bodyLatex: If instead each ball is independently white or black with probability $\dfrac{1}{2}$, the priors are $\dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $P(W) = \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot 1 = \dfrac{2}{3}$ as well.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

verification.note: SymPy: total probability gives 2/3 under both the uniform-composition and independent-colour priors.

jelet-2025-q016.conceptSummary: Power of a point: for any secant through $P$, $PA \cdot PB = S_{1} = x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} - r^{2}$.

steps.title: Power of the point
steps.bodyLatex: For every line through $P$ meeting the circle at $A$ and $B$, $PA \cdot PB = S(3, 11)$ (it equals the square of the tangent length from $P$).

verification.note: SymPy: for a symbolic direction (cos t, sin t), the product of the two roots of |P + s(cos t, sin t)|^2 = 9 equals 121.

jelet-2025-q017.conceptSummary: Compare the right- and left-hand derivatives at $x = 0$.

steps.title: Value at $0$
steps.bodyLatex: $f(0) = a\cdot 0 + b e^{0} + c\cdot 0 = b$.

steps.title: Differentiability condition
steps.bodyLatex: $Rf'(0) = Lf'(0) \Rightarrow 2a + 3b = -(2a + 3b) \Rightarrow 2a + 3b = 0$ ($c$ is unrestricted because $c|2x|^{3}$ is differentiable at $0$).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) $2a + 3b = 0$.

verification.note: SymPy: one-sided limits of the difference quotient are 2a+3b and -(2a+3b); equal iff 2a+3b = 0.

jelet-2025-q018.conceptSummary: The even part of $a^{x}$ is $g(x) = \dfrac{a^{x} + a^{-x}}{2}$; expand the required sum.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: The two expressions are identical, so $g(x+y) + g(x-y) = 2g(x)g(y)$. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: with g = (a^x + a^-x)/2, simplify(g(x+y) + g(x-y) - 2g(x)g(y)) = 0.

jelet-2025-q019.conceptSummary: $\vec{c}$ lies in the plane of $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$, so a vector perpendicular to both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ is normal to that plane, i.e. parallel to $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$.

steps.title: Locate $\vec{d}$
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ are non-parallel ($\vec{c} \perp \vec{a}$) and both lie in the plane of $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$. Hence $\vec{d} \perp \vec{a}, \vec{c}$ means $\vec{d}$ is normal to that plane: $\vec{d} \parallel \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$.

steps.title: Compute the normal
steps.bodyLatex: $(\vec{i} + \vec{j} - \vec{k}) \times (\vec{i} - \vec{j} + \vec{k}) = \begin{vmatrix} \vec{i} & \vec{j} & \vec{k} \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0\,\vec{i} - 2\vec{j} - 2\vec{k}$.

steps.title: Normalise
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec{d} = \pm\dfrac{-2\vec{j} - 2\vec{k}}{2\sqrt{2}} = \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\vec{j} + \vec{k}\right)$.

steps.title: Explicit check
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec{c} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\left(2\vec{i} - \vec{j} + \vec{k}\right)$ (component of $\vec{b}$ perpendicular to $\vec{a}$, normalised). Then $(\vec{j} + \vec{k})\cdot(\vec{i} + \vec{j} - \vec{k}) = 0$ and $(\vec{j} + \vec{k})\cdot(2\vec{i} - \vec{j} + \vec{k}) = 0$. Answer: (B) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\vec{j} + \vec{k}\right)$.

verification.note: SymPy: c = normalised (b - proj_a b) = (2,-1,1)/sqrt6; d = a x c normalised = ±(0,1,1)/sqrt2; options A, C, D fail perpendicularity.

jelet-2025-q020.conceptSummary: The square of the tangent length from $(x_{1}, y_{1})$ to $S = 0$ equals $S(x_{1}, y_{1})$.

steps.title: Point on the first circle
steps.bodyLatex: If $(x_{1}, y_{1})$ lies on the first circle, then $x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} = -\alpha$.

steps.title: Tangent length to the second circle
Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: $L = \sqrt{\beta - \alpha}$ (real when $\beta > \alpha$, i.e. the first circle encloses the concentric second one). Answer: (C) $\sqrt{\beta - \alpha}$.

verification.note: SymPy: substituting x1^2+y1^2+2g x1+2f y1 = -alpha into S2 gives beta - alpha identically.
SymPy: exact integer computation of det(A^2009 - 5*A^2008) = -6.

jelet-2025-q022.conceptSummary: A homogeneous system has a non-trivial solution iff its coefficient determinant is $0$.

steps.title: Real roots
steps.bodyLatex: $r^{2} + 2r + 2 = (r + 1)^{2} + 1 > 0$ has no real root, so the only real solution is $r = 2$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) $2$.

verification.note: SymPy: det = 2r^3 - 4r - 8 = 2(r-2)(r^2+2r+2); only real root r = 2.

steps.title: Expand
steps.bodyLatex: $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^{2} = |\vec{a}|^{2} + |\vec{b}|^{2} - 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 2 - 2\cos\theta$.

steps.title: Half-angle identity
steps.bodyLatex: $2 - 2\cos\theta = 4\sin^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, so $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}| = 2\left|\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right|$.

steps.title: Sign
steps.bodyLatex: $0 \leq \theta \leq \pi \Rightarrow 0 \leq \dfrac{\theta}{2} \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2} \geq 0$ and $\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) $\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\vec{a} - \vec{b}\right|$.

verification.note: SymPy: with a = (1,0), b = (cos t, sin t), |a-b|^2/4 - sin^2(t/2) simplifies to 0.

steps.title: Use $\sin(\pi - t) = \sin t$
steps.bodyLatex: $\pi\cos^{2}x = \pi - \pi\sin^{2}x$, so $\sin\left(\pi\cos^{2}x\right) = \sin\left(\pi\sin^{2}x\right)$.

steps.title: Rearrange
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{\sin\left(\pi\sin^{2}x\right)}{x^{2}} = \dfrac{\sin\left(\pi\sin^{2}x\right)}{\pi\sin^{2}x}\cdot\pi\cdot\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right)^{2}$.

steps.title: Take the limit
steps.bodyLatex: As $x \to 0$, $\pi\sin^{2}x \to 0$, so the limit is $1 \cdot \pi \cdot 1^{2} = \pi$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $\pi$.

verification.note: SymPy: limit(sin(pi*cos(x)^2)/x^2, x, 0) = pi.

jelet-2025-q025.conceptSummary: Show $y' \geq 0$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with equality only at the isolated point $x = 0$.

steps.title: Differentiate term by term
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(2x) = 2$, $\dfrac{d}{dx}\cot^{-1}x = -\dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}$, $\dfrac{d}{dx}\log\left(\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - x\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}} - 1}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - x} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}$.

steps.title: Combine
steps.bodyLatex: $y' = 2 - \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}} = \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\right) + \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}\right)$.

steps.title: Sign of $y'$
steps.bodyLatex: Both brackets are $\geq 0$ for all real $x$ (since $1 + x^{2} \geq 1$), and both vanish only at $x = 0$. Hence $y' > 0$ for $x \neq 0$ and $y'(0) = 0$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: A derivative that is positive except at one isolated point makes $y$ strictly increasing on the whole real line $(-\infty, \infty)$; (A) and (C) are false, and (B) is only the restriction of this result to $[0, \infty)$. Answer: (D) increases on $(-\infty, \infty)$.

verification.note: SymPy: y' - [(1 - 1/(1+x^2)) + (1 - 1/sqrt(1+x^2))] simplifies to 0; y'(0) = 0 and y' > 0 at sampled x != 0.

jelet-2025-q026.conceptSummary: Maximise the inscribed cylinder's volume using similar triangles, then compare it with the cone's volume.

steps.title: Set up the geometry
steps.bodyLatex: Let the cone have base radius $R$ and height $H$, so $p = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi R^{2}H$. A cylinder of radius $r$ ($0 < r < R$) inscribed coaxially has height $h$ with $\dfrac{h}{H} = \dfrac{R - r}{R}$ (similar triangles), i.e. $h = H\left(1 - \dfrac{r}{R}\right)$.

steps.title: Volume of the cylinder
steps.bodyLatex: $V(r) = \pi r^{2}h = \pi H\left(r^{2} - \dfrac{r^{3}}{R}\right)$.

steps.title: Maximise
steps.bodyLatex: $V'(r) = \pi H\left(2r - \dfrac{3r^{2}}{R}\right) = 0 \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{2R}{3}$, and $V''\!\left(\tfrac{2R}{3}\right) = \pi H\left(2 - \dfrac{6r}{R}\right) = -2\pi H < 0$, so this is a maximum.

steps.title: Largest volume
steps.bodyLatex: $q = \pi\cdot\dfrac{4R^{2}}{9}\cdot\dfrac{H}{3} = \dfrac{4}{27}\pi R^{2}H = \dfrac{4}{9}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}\pi R^{2}H = \dfrac{4}{9}p$.

verification.note: SymPy: V(r) = pi H (r^2 - r^3/R) has its maximum at r = 2R/3; p/q simplifies to 9/4.

jelet-2025-q027.conceptSummary: A line perpendicular to $x + 2y = 0$ has slope $2$; apply the tangency condition $c^{2} = a^{2}m^{2} - b^{2}$.

steps.title: Slope of the tangents
steps.bodyLatex: $x + 2y = 0$ has slope $-\dfrac{1}{2}$, so a perpendicular line has slope $m = 2$: $y = 2x + c$.

steps.title: Tangency condition
steps.bodyLatex: Substitute into $3x^{2} - 4y^{2} = 12$: $3x^{2} - 4(2x + c)^{2} = 12 \Rightarrow 13x^{2} + 16cx + 4c^{2} + 12 = 0$. For tangency the discriminant is zero: $256c^{2} - 52(4c^{2} + 12) = 0 \Rightarrow 48c^{2} = 624 \Rightarrow c^{2} = 13$. (Same as $c^{2} = a^{2}m^{2} - b^{2} = 4\cdot 4 - 3$.)

steps.title: Tangents
steps.bodyLatex: $y = 2x \pm \sqrt{13}$.

steps.title: Check the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $y = 13 \pm 2x$ and (D) $y = 7 \pm 2x$ include slope $-2$ and the wrong intercepts; (C) uses $c^{2} = 19 = 16 + 3$, the ellipse-type sign error. Answer: (B) $y = 2x \pm \sqrt{13}$.

verification.note: SymPy: discriminant of 3x^2 - 4(2x+c)^2 - 12 vanishes iff c^2 = 13; only option B lists exactly {(2, sqrt13), (2, -sqrt13)}.

jelet-2025-q028.conceptSummary: Sum the series by differentiating a geometric series; then $f(x) = \dfrac{2x}{(1 - x^{2})^{2}}$ integrates by substitution.

steps.title: Recognise a derivative
steps.bodyLatex: $2x + 4x^{3} + \ldots + 2nx^{2n-1} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{2} + x^{4} + \ldots + x^{2n}\right)$.

steps.title: Take the limit
steps.bodyLatex: For $0 < x < 1$: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} x^{2k} = \dfrac{x^{2}}{1 - x^{2}}$, and the differentiated series converges uniformly on compact subsets of $(-1,1)$, so $f(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{x^{2}}{1 - x^{2}} = \dfrac{2x}{(1 - x^{2})^{2}}$.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.bodyLatex: Put $u = 1 - x^{2}$, $du = -2x\,dx$: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{2x}{(1 - x^{2})^{2}}dx = -\int u^{-2}\,du = \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}}$ (+ constant).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Differentiating (A) gives $\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$, (B) gives $\dfrac{x}{(1-x^{2})^{3/2}}$ and (D) gives $0$; none equals $f$. Answer: (C) $\dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}}$.

verification.note: SymPy: summation(2k x^(2k-1), k=1..oo) = 2x/(1-x^2)^2 for |x|<1; d/dx[1/(1-x^2)] equals it, the other options do not.

jelet-2025-q029.conceptSummary: Differentiate the given solution and subtract $y/x$; rewrite the remainder in terms of $x/y$.

steps.title: Differentiate the solution
steps.bodyLatex: $y = \dfrac{x}{\log(cx)} \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\log(cx) - x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}}{\log^{2}(cx)} = \dfrac{1}{\log(cx)} - \dfrac{1}{\log^{2}(cx)}$.

steps.title: Express in $x$ and $y$
steps.bodyLatex: From the solution $\dfrac{1}{\log(cx)} = \dfrac{y}{x}$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}$.

steps.title: Compare with the equation
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} + \phi(x/y)$ gives $\phi(x/y) = -\dfrac{y^{2}}{x^{2}} = -\dfrac{1}{(x/y)^{2}}$, a function of $x/y$ as required.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) $-\dfrac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}$.

verification.note: SymPy: with y = x/log(cx), simplify(y' - y/x + y^2/x^2) = 0; options B, C, D leave a non-zero residual.

jelet-2025-q030.conceptSummary: With indistinguishable coins the observable outcomes are the unordered results $\{HH, HT, TT\}$, taken as equally likely.

steps.title: Sample space for indistinguishable coins
steps.bodyLatex: When the two coins cannot be told apart, the outcome is only the number of heads: $\{\text{two heads},\ \text{one head and one tail},\ \text{two tails}\}$. The question treats these $3$ outcomes as the equally likely sample space.

steps.title: Favourable outcomes
steps.bodyLatex: Exactly one outcome, $\{H, T\}$, has one head and one tail.

steps.title: Conclusion and remark
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) $\dfrac{1}{3}$ (official key). Remark: if the coins are physically fair and are labelled (distinguishable), the four ordered outcomes $HH, HT, TH, TT$ are equally likely and the probability would be $\dfrac{1}{2}$. The word ``indistinguishable'' in the stem signals the unordered (Bose–Einstein) count the setters intended.

verification.note: SymPy/itertools: combinations_with_replacement('HT', 2) gives 3 equally likely unordered outcomes, 1 favourable -> 1/3 (key B); ordered count 2/4 = 1/2 shown for contrast.

jelet-2025-q031.conceptSummary: Use $A(\operatorname{adj} A) = (\operatorname{adj} A)A = |A|I_{n}$ with $n = 3$; evaluate all four statements.

steps.title: (B) The fundamental identity
steps.bodyLatex: For every square matrix, $A(\operatorname{adj} A) = |A|I_{3}$ (cofactor expansion along rows; off-diagonal entries are expansions with alien cofactors and vanish). (B) is TRUE.

steps.title: (A) Determinant of the adjoint
steps.bodyLatex: Take determinants: $|A|\,|\operatorname{adj} A| = \left||A|I_{3}\right| = |A|^{3}$. If $|A| \neq 0$, divide: $|\operatorname{adj} A| = |A|^{2}$. (A) is TRUE.

steps.title: (C) Invertibility of $A$
steps.bodyLatex: If $|A| \neq 0$, then $B = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A$ satisfies $AB = BA = I_{3}$, so $A$ is invertible. (C) is TRUE.

steps.title: (D) Invertibility of $\operatorname{adj} A$
steps.bodyLatex: By (A), $|\operatorname{adj} A| = |A|^{2} \neq 0$ when $|A| \neq 0$, so $\operatorname{adj} A$ is invertible, with $(\operatorname{adj} A)^{-1} = \dfrac{A}{|A|}$. (D) is TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: All four statements hold. Answer: (A), (B), (C), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: for a generic symbolic 3x3 A, A*adj(A) - det(A) I = 0 and det(adj A) - det(A)^2 = 0 identically; inverse checks pass for nonsingular samples.

jelet-2025-q032.conceptSummary: Squeeze $x^{2}\sin(1/x)$ for continuity and differentiability; then examine the limit of $f'(x)$ as $x \to 0$.

steps.title: (B) Continuity at $0$
steps.bodyLatex: $|x^{2}\sin(1/x)| \leq x^{2} \to 0$, so $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0} f(x) = 0 = f(0)$. (B) is TRUE.

steps.title: (C) Derivability at $0$
steps.bodyLatex: $f'(0) = \displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{h^{2}\sin(1/h) - 0}{h} = \lim_{h\to0} h\sin(1/h) = 0$ (since $|h\sin(1/h)| \leq |h|$). (C) is TRUE.

steps.title: $f'$ near $0$
steps.bodyLatex: For $x \neq 0$: $f'(x) = 2x\sin\dfrac{1}{x} - \cos\dfrac{1}{x}$. Along $x_{n} = \dfrac{1}{2n\pi}$, $f'(x_{n}) = -1$; along $y_{n} = \dfrac{1}{(2n+1)\pi}$, $f'(y_{n}) = +1$. Both sequences tend to $0$, so $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0} f'(x)$ does not exist and $f'$ is not continuous at $0$.

steps.title: (A) and (D)
steps.bodyLatex: (A) claims $f'$ is continuous at $0$ — FALSE. (D) says $f$ is derivable at $0$ but $f'$ is not continuous there — TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B), (C), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: limit(x^2 sin(1/x), x, 0) = 0, limit(h sin(1/h), h, 0) = 0; f'(1/(2n pi)) = -1 and f'(1/((2n+1) pi)) = 1, so f' has no limit at 0.

jelet-2025-q033.conceptSummary: The integrand is the derivative of a quotient: recognise $\dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{x^{7}}{2x^{7} + x^{2} + 1}$.

steps.title: Substitute
steps.bodyLatex: Let $t = 2 + x^{-5} + x^{-7}$; then $dt = -\left(5x^{-6} + 7x^{-8}\right)dx$, so $I = -\displaystyle\int t^{-2}\,dt = \dfrac{1}{t} + c_{1} = \dfrac{x^{7}}{2x^{7} + x^{2} + 1} + c_{1}$.

steps.title: (B), (C)
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{x^{5}}{x^{2} + 1 + 2x^{7}}$ has numerator $5x^{4}(x^{2}+1+2x^{7}) - x^{5}(2x + 14x^{6}) = -4x^{11} + 3x^{6} + 5x^{4}$ and $\dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{1}{x^{2}+1+2x^{7}}$ has numerator $-(2x + 14x^{6})$; neither equals $5x^{8} + 7x^{6}$, and two antiderivatives can differ only by a constant, which these do not. FALSE.

steps.title: (D)
steps.bodyLatex: The antiderivative in (A) is $\dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)} + c_{1}$ with $p = x^{7}$ and $q = 2x^{7} + x^{2} + 1$, both of degree $7$. (D) is TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: d/dx[x^7/(2x^7+x^2+1)] - integrand = 0; options B, C differ from the integrand by a non-constant; deg p = deg q = 7 for option A.

jelet-2025-q034.conceptSummary: Treat the equation as a quadratic in $p = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$ and factor it.

steps.title: Factor
steps.bodyLatex: $p^{2} - (e^{x} + e^{-x})p + 1 = 0$. Since $e^{x}\cdot e^{-x} = 1$ and $e^{x} + e^{-x}$ is their sum, $(p - e^{x})(p - e^{-x}) = 0$.

steps.title: First branch
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x} \Rightarrow y = e^{x} + c$, i.e. $y - e^{x} = c$ — option (D). TRUE.

steps.title: Second branch
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{-x} \Rightarrow y = -e^{-x} + c$ — option (A). TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: factor(p^2 - (e^x+e^-x)p + 1) = (p - e^x)(p - e^-x); substituting y' from each option leaves 0 only for A and D.

jelet-2025-q035.conceptSummary: Check the left piece's derivative, the junction value, the one-sided derivatives at $x = 2$ and the values on $(2, 3]$.

steps.title: (A) Monotonicity on $[-1, 2]$
steps.bodyLatex: $f'(x) = 6x + 12 = 6(x + 2) \geq 6 > 0$ for $-1 \leq x \leq 2$, so $f$ is increasing there. TRUE.

steps.title: (B) Continuity on $[-1, 3]$
steps.bodyLatex: Each piece is a polynomial. At $x = 2$: $f(2) = 12 + 24 - 1 = 35$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2^{+}}(37 - x) = 35$. So $f$ is continuous on $[-1, 3]$. TRUE.

steps.title: (C) Derivative at $2$
steps.bodyLatex: Left derivative $= 6(2) + 12 = 24$; right derivative $= \dfrac{d}{dx}(37 - x) = -1$. They differ, so $f'(2)$ does not exist. TRUE.

steps.title: (D) Maximum at $x = 2$
steps.bodyLatex: On $[-1, 2]$, $f$ increases to $f(2) = 35$; on $(2, 3]$, $37 - x < 35$ and decreases. Hence the maximum value $35$ occurs at $x = 2$. TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A), (B), (C), (D).

steps.title: Bound the greatest-integer part
steps.bodyLatex: For $x \neq 0$: $\dfrac{1}{x^{3}} - 1 < \left[\dfrac{1}{x^{3}}\right] \leq \dfrac{1}{x^{3}}$.

steps.title: Multiply by $x^{8} > 0$
steps.bodyLatex: $x^{5} - x^{8} < x^{8}\left[\dfrac{1}{x^{3}}\right] \leq x^{5}$ on both sides of $0$.

steps.title: Squeeze
steps.bodyLatex: Both bounds tend to $0$ as $x \to 0$, so $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0} x^{8}\left[\dfrac{1}{x^{3}}\right] = 0$.

steps.title: Evaluate each option
steps.bodyLatex: The limit is $0$: (A) non-zero — FALSE; (B) rational — TRUE ($0 = 0/1$); (C) strictly positive integer — FALSE; (D) zero — TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: limit(x^5 - x^8) = limit(x^5) = 0 from both sides; 0 is rational, not positive, not non-zero.

jelet-2025-q037.conceptSummary: Independence gives $P(E)P(F) = \dfrac{1}{12}$ and $(1 - P(E))(1 - P(F)) = \dfrac{1}{2}$; solve the symmetric system.

steps.title: Write the equations
steps.bodyLatex: Let $P(E) = u$, $P(F) = v$. Independence: $uv = \dfrac{1}{12}$. Complements of independent events are independent: $(1 - u)(1 - v) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

steps.title: Find the sum
steps.bodyLatex: $1 - (u + v) + uv = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow u + v = 1 + \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{7}{12}$.

steps.title: Evaluate each option
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $\left(\tfrac{1}{3}, \tfrac{1}{4}\right)$ — TRUE. (D) $\left(\tfrac{1}{4}, \tfrac{1}{3}\right)$ — TRUE. (B) $\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{6} = \tfrac{1}{12}$ but $\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{5}{6} = \tfrac{5}{12} \neq \tfrac{1}{2}$ — FALSE. (C) same pair reversed — FALSE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: solve([u v - 1/12, (1-u)(1-v) - 1/2]) = {(1/3, 1/4), (1/4, 1/3)}; options B and C violate the second equation.

jelet-2025-q038.conceptSummary: Two distinct intersection points $\iff$ distance from the centre to the line is less than $r$ $\iff |c| < r\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}$; test which options are sufficient.

steps.title: Condition for two points
steps.bodyLatex: The distance from $(0,0)$ to $mx - y + c = 0$ is $\dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}$. Two distinct points $\iff \dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}} < r \iff -r\sqrt{1 + m^{2}} < c < r\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}$. (Equivalently, the discriminant of $(1 + m^{2})x^{2} + 2mcx + c^{2} - r^{2} = 0$ is $4\left[r^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2}\right] > 0$.)

steps.title: (A) and (B)
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $-r\sqrt{1 + m^{2}} < c \leq 0$ and (B) $0 \leq c < r\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}$ are the two halves of this interval, so each guarantees two distinct points. Both TRUE.

steps.title: (C)
steps.bodyLatex: $-c\sqrt{1 - m^{2}} < r$ is not sufficient: with $m = 0$, $r = 1$, $c = 5$ it holds ($-5 < 1$) but $|c| = 5 > 1$, so the line misses the circle. FALSE.

steps.title: (D)
steps.bodyLatex: $r < c\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}$: with $m = 0$, $r = 1$, $c = 2$ it holds, yet $|c| > r$ and there is no intersection. FALSE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A), (B).

verification.note: SymPy: discriminant = 4[r^2(1+m^2) - c^2]; A and B imply it is positive; counterexamples (m,r,c) = (0,1,5) for C and (0,1,2) for D.

jelet-2025-q039.conceptSummary: The coefficient matrix is the circulant $\begin{bmatrix} a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b \end{bmatrix}$ with $\Delta = -(a + b + c)\left(a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} - ab - bc - ca\right)$, and the right-hand sides add to $0$.

steps.title: Determinant and a key identity
steps.bodyLatex: $\Delta = 3abc - a^{3} - b^{3} - c^{3} = -\dfrac{1}{2}(a + b + c)\left[(a - b)^{2} + (b - c)^{2} + (c - a)^{2}\right]$. Also each column of the matrix sums to $a + b + c$, and the right-hand sides satisfy $(q - r) + (r - p) + (p - q) = 0$.

steps.title: (A) $p = q = r$
steps.bodyLatex: All right-hand sides are $0$: the system is homogeneous and $x = y = z = 0$ is always a solution. TRUE.

steps.title: (C) $a, b, c$ distinct and $a + b + c = 0$
steps.bodyLatex: Then $\Delta = 0$, but $(a-b)^{2} + (b-c)^{2} + (c-a)^{2} > 0$ means the matrix has rank $2$ (its nonzero eigenvalues are $a + b\omega + c\omega^{2}$ and its conjugate). Adding the three equations gives $(a + b + c)(x + y + z) = 0$, i.e. $0 = 0$, which is the only dependency among the rows, and the right-hand sides satisfy it. So the augmented matrix also has rank $2$ and the system is consistent (infinitely many solutions). TRUE.

steps.title: (D)
steps.bodyLatex: (A) already gives a consistent case, and for $a + b + c \neq 0$ with $a, b, c$ not all equal, $\Delta \neq 0$ gives a unique solution. FALSE.

steps.title: (B) $a = b = c$ and $p \neq q \neq r$ — official key versus mathematics
steps.bodyLatex: With $a = b = c = k$, every left-hand side equals $k(x + y + z)$, so a solution needs $q - r = r - p = p - q$; these three numbers sum to $0$, so all would be $0$, forcing $p = q = r$. Since $p \neq q$, the system is inconsistent (this also holds for $k = 0$, and under the reading $p = r \neq q$). So statement (B) is also mathematically true. The official WBJEEB key (JEEB/Reg-171/25) nevertheless lists only (A) and (C). The stored key is kept exactly as published, and this discrepancy is recorded for candidates.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Official answer: (A), (C). Note: by the derivation above, (B) is also a true statement; the key omits it.

verification.note: SymPy: det = 3abc - a^3 - b^3 - c^3; A: homogeneous; C: rank(M) = rank([M|b]) = 2 for distinct a+b+c=0 samples; D false. B is ALSO true (linsolve empty for a=b=c, p!=q); recorded as a documented key dispute in verify_solutions_sympy.py.

jelet-2025-q040.conceptSummary: Use the substitution $x \to \dfrac{1}{x}$, which maps $\left[\tfrac{1}{a}, a\right]$ to itself, and $\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for $x > 0$.

steps.title: Substitute $x = 1/t$
steps.bodyLatex: $dx = -\dfrac{dt}{t^{2}}$, $\dfrac{dx}{x} = -\dfrac{dt}{t}$, and the limits $\tfrac{1}{a} \to a$, $a \to \tfrac{1}{a}$. So $I = \displaystyle\int_{1/a}^{a}\dfrac{\tan^{-1}(1/t)}{t}\,dt$ (taking $a > 0$).

steps.title: Add the two forms
steps.bodyLatex: $2I = \displaystyle\int_{1/a}^{a}\dfrac{\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}(1/x)}{x}\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\int_{1/a}^{a}\dfrac{dx}{x}$.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.bodyLatex: $\displaystyle\int_{1/a}^{a}\dfrac{dx}{x} = \log a - \log\dfrac{1}{a} = 2\log a$, so $2I = \pi\log a$ and $I = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\log a$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\log a$.

verification.note: SymPy: dI/da = atan(a)/a + atan(1/a)/a simplifies to pi/(2a) with I(1) = 0, so I = (pi/2) log a; numeric quadrature at a = 2, 3, 5 agrees.

jelet-2025-q041.conceptSummary: Terms added together must have the same dimensions: $\dfrac{a}{V^{2}}$ has the dimensions of pressure, so $[a] = [P][V^{2}]$.

steps.title: Principle of homogeneity
steps.bodyLatex: In $\left(P + \dfrac{a}{V^{2}}\right)$, a quantity can only be added to one of the same kind, so $\left[\dfrac{a}{V^{2}}\right] = [P]$.

steps.title: Compare with the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) is printed as $[MT^{5}T^{-2}]$ (no length; it reduces to $MT^{3}$), (B) $ML^{-1}T^{-2}$ is the dimension of $P$ itself, (C) $L^{3}$ is the dimension of $b$, (D) is $L^{6}$. None equals $ML^{5}T^{-2}$. Because no option is correct (option (A) is a misprint of the intended $[ML^{5}T^{-2}]$), WBJEEB withdrew the question in the final answer key.

steps.title: Marking
steps.bodyLatex: Q41 is a Category-I item marked W (withdrawn). As a withdrawn Category-I question it awards the full $+1$ mark ($+12$ twelfths) to every candidate, whatever they marked.

verification.note: SymPy: dimension exponents (M, L, T) of P*V^2 = (1, 5, -2); options encode (1,0,3), (1,-1,-2), (0,3,0), (0,6,0); no match -> withdrawn (W), +1 mark (+12 twelfths) to all.

jelet-2025-q042.conceptSummary: For a quotient $R = V/I$ the maximum relative errors add.

steps.title: Relative errors
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = \dfrac{5}{100} = 5\%$ and $\dfrac{\Delta I}{I} = \dfrac{0{\cdot}2}{10} = 2\%$.

steps.title: Combine
steps.bodyLatex: $\ln R = \ln V - \ln I \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta R}{R} \leq \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + \dfrac{\Delta I}{I}$ (worst case, errors add in magnitude).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) $7\%$.

jelet-2025-q043.conceptSummary: $\overline{A}$ is perpendicular to both $\overline{B}$ and $\overline{C}$, hence parallel to their cross product.

steps.title: Interpret the conditions
steps.bodyLatex: $\overline{A}\cdot\overline{B} = 0$ and $\overline{A}\cdot\overline{C} = 0$ mean $\overline{A}$ is perpendicular to both $\overline{B}$ and $\overline{C}$.

steps.title: Direction perpendicular to both
steps.bodyLatex: For non-parallel $\overline{B}, \overline{C}$, the only direction perpendicular to both is that of $\overline{B}\times\overline{C}$, since $(\overline{B}\times\overline{C})\cdot\overline{B} = (\overline{B}\times\overline{C})\cdot\overline{C} = 0$. So $\overline{A} = \lambda(\overline{B}\times\overline{C})$.

steps.title: Reject the others
steps.bodyLatex: $\overline{A} \parallel \overline{C}$ would give $\overline{A}\cdot\overline{C} = \lambda|\overline{C}|^{2} \neq 0$; similarly for $\overline{B}$. $\overline{B}\cdot\overline{C}$ is a scalar, not a vector, so (D) is meaningless.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $\overline{B}\times\overline{C}$.

verification.note: SymPy: for generic B, C, (B x C).B = (B x C).C = 0 identically; C.C and B.B are non-zero; B.C is a scalar.

jelet-2025-q044.conceptSummary: Read $a(t) = 2t - 2$ from the graph and integrate with $v(0) = 0$: $v = t^{2} - 2t$.

steps.title: Equation of the acceleration line
steps.bodyLatex: The graph is a straight line with $a = -2$ at $t = 0$ and $a = 0$ at $t = 1$, so its slope is $2\ \text{m/s}^{3}$ and $a(t) = 2t - 2$.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.bodyLatex: $v(t) = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}(2\tau - 2)\,d\tau = t^{2} - 2t = t(t - 2)$, using $v(0) = 0$.

steps.title: Shape of $v(t)$
steps.bodyLatex: An upward-opening parabola: $v = 0$ at $t = 0$, $v < 0$ for $0 < t < 2$ with minimum $v(1) = -1$ (where $a = 0$), $v = 0$ again at $t = 2$, and $v$ rising ever faster afterwards since $a > 0$ grows.

steps.title: Match the graphs
steps.bodyLatex: (A) is the mirror image (positive arch), which would need $a = 2 - 2t$. (B) and (D) are piecewise-linear, which would need piecewise-constant acceleration. Graph (C) dips below the axis to a minimum at $t = 1$, crosses at $t = 2$ and then rises steeply. Answer: (C).

verification.note: SymPy: integrate(2t - 2, (t, 0, t)) = t^2 - 2t; the verifier fits the plotted curve of each option SVG and only option C is an upward parabola with its vertex at the dotted t = 1 line, below the axis.

steps.title: Resultant force
steps.bodyLatex: $\overline{F} = (2 + 1)\hat{i} + (3 - 2)\hat{j} + (-1 + 2)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ N.

steps.title: Displacement
steps.bodyLatex: $\overline{d} = (1 - 0)\hat{i} + (1 - 0)\hat{j} + (2 - 1)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ m.

steps.title: Work
steps.bodyLatex: $W = \overline{F}\cdot\overline{d} = 3 + 1 + 1 = 5$ J (constant forces, so the path does not matter).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $5$ J.

jelet-2025-q046.conceptSummary: Acceleration is the curvature of the $x$–$t$ graph; it is zero where the graph is a straight line.

steps.title: Relation used
steps.bodyLatex: $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$ is the slope of the displacement–time graph and $a = \dfrac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}}$ is the rate of change of that slope.

steps.title: Examine each region
steps.bodyLatex: AB: a straight rising line, so constant slope and $a = 0$. BC: curved (slope changes from negative to positive), so $a \neq 0$. CD: a straight falling line, so constant (negative) velocity and $a = 0$. DE: curved (slope decreasing toward zero), so $a \neq 0$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Acceleration is zero in AB and CD. Answer: (B) AB and CD.

verification.note: Verifier parses the redrawn SVG path: segments AB and CD are straight 'L' commands, BC and DE are cubic curves with non-collinear control points -> zero acceleration only in AB, CD.

jelet-2025-q047.conceptSummary: Free-fall time from rest depends only on height; after the stone is stopped it restarts from rest at the remaining height.

steps.title: Distance in the first $3$ s
steps.bodyLatex: $s_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}g(3)^{2} = \dfrac{9g}{2}$, so the remaining height is $\dfrac{25g}{2} - \dfrac{9g}{2} = 8g$.

steps.title: Time for the rest, starting from rest
steps.bodyLatex: $8g = \dfrac{1}{2}g t_{2}^{2} \Rightarrow t_{2}^{2} = 16 \Rightarrow t_{2} = 4$ s.

steps.title: Total
steps.bodyLatex: Fall time $= 3 + 4 = 7$ s (the duration of the stop is not counted). Answer: (C) $7{\cdot}0$ sec.

verification.note: SymPy: solve(8g = g t^2/2, t>0) = 4; 3 + 4 = 7.

jelet-2025-q048.conceptSummary: Net downward force = weight − buoyant force; divide by the stone's mass.

steps.title: Forces
steps.bodyLatex: Let the stone have volume $V$, density $\rho\sigma_{w}$ ($\sigma_{w}$ = density of water, $\rho$ = relative density). Weight $= \rho\sigma_{w}Vg$; buoyant force $= \sigma_{w}Vg$ (Archimedes).

steps.title: Newton's second law
steps.bodyLatex: $(\rho\sigma_{w}V)a = \rho\sigma_{w}Vg - \sigma_{w}Vg$.

steps.title: Solve
steps.bodyLatex: $a = g\dfrac{\rho - 1}{\rho} = g\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\rho}\right)$ (positive, i.e. sinking, when $\rho > 1$).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $g\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\rho}\right)$.

verification.note: SymPy: solve(rho s V a - rho s V g + s V g, a) = g(1 - 1/rho).

jelet-2025-q049.conceptSummary: For a circular orbit $K = \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$, $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}$, so $E = -\dfrac{GMm}{2r}$ and $U = 2E$.

steps.title: Orbital speed
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} = \dfrac{GMm}{r^{2}} \Rightarrow K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$.

steps.title: Total energy
steps.bodyLatex: $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}$, so $E_{0} = K + U = -\dfrac{GMm}{2r}$.

steps.title: Potential energy in terms of $E_{0}$
steps.bodyLatex: $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r} = 2\left(-\dfrac{GMm}{2r}\right) = 2E_{0}$ (and $K = -E_{0}$).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $2E_{0}$.

verification.note: SymPy: with v^2 = GM/r, U/(K+U) simplifies to 2.

jelet-2025-q050.conceptSummary: The bomb starts at rest, so the total momentum stays zero; with equal masses the three velocities sum to zero.

steps.title: Momentum conservation
steps.bodyLatex: $m\vec{v}_{1} + m\vec{v}_{2} + m\vec{v}_{3} = \vec{0} \Rightarrow \vec{v}_{3} = -(\vec{v}_{1} + \vec{v}_{2})$.

steps.title: Third fragment
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec{v}_{3} = -3\hat{i} + \hat{j}$ m/s. (Option (B) is $\vec{v}_{1} + \vec{v}_{2}$ itself — the sign trap.)

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) $(-3\hat{i} + \hat{j})$ m/s.

jelet-2025-q051.conceptSummary: Viscous drag $6\pi\eta r v$ grows with speed until it balances the effective weight, so $v$ rises from $0$ and approaches a terminal value.

steps.title: Equation of motion
steps.bodyLatex: For a sphere of radius $r$, density $\rho$ in a fluid of density $\sigma$ and viscosity $\eta$: $m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = mg - \tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\sigma g - 6\pi\eta r v$.

steps.title: Solve with $v(0) = 0$
steps.bodyLatex: Writing $\tau = \dfrac{m}{6\pi\eta r}$ and $v_{t} = \dfrac{2r^{2}(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta}$: $v(t) = v_{t}\left(1 - e^{-t/\tau}\right)$.

steps.title: Shape of the graph
steps.bodyLatex: $v(0) = 0$ (body just dropped); $\dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{v_{t}}{\tau}e^{-t/\tau} > 0$ so $v$ increases monotonically; $\dfrac{dv}{dt} \to 0$ and $v \to v_{t}$, a constant terminal velocity.

steps.title: Match the graphs
steps.bodyLatex: (B) starts with a non-zero speed, (C) slows back to zero, and (D) speeds up again after levelling off — none is possible once drag balances the weight. Graph (A) starts at $0$, rises and flattens to a constant value. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: dsolve(m v' = m g' - k v, v(0)=0) = v_t (1 - exp(-t/tau)); verifier reads each option SVG: only (A) starts at v = 0, is monotone and ends flat.

jelet-2025-q052.conceptSummary: No external horizontal force acts on bullet + block, so momentum is conserved; a perfectly inelastic impact dissipates kinetic energy.

steps.title: Momentum
steps.bodyLatex: The surface is frictionless and gravity/normal forces are vertical, so the horizontal momentum of the system is conserved: $mu = (m + M)v_{f}$.

steps.title: Kinetic energy
steps.bodyLatex: $KE_{i} = \tfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}$, $KE_{f} = \tfrac{1}{2}(m + M)v_{f}^{2} = \dfrac{m}{m + M}KE_{i} < KE_{i}$. The difference $\dfrac{M}{m + M}KE_{i}$ goes into heat, sound and deformation as the bullet embeds.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Only momentum is conserved. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: v_f = m u/(m+M); KE_f/KE_i simplifies to m/(m+M) < 1 for M > 0.

jelet-2025-q053.conceptSummary: For a rod of uniform cross-section the mass per unit length is proportional to $\rho(x) = \rho_{0}x^{2}/L^{2}$; use $x_{cm} = \dfrac{\int x\,dm}{\int dm}$.

steps.title: Mass element
steps.bodyLatex: With cross-section $A$: $dm = A\rho_{0}\dfrac{x^{2}}{L^{2}}dx$, $0 \leq x \leq L$.

steps.title: Integrals
steps.bodyLatex: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{L} dm = \dfrac{A\rho_{0}}{L^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{L^{3}}{3}$ and $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{L} x\,dm = \dfrac{A\rho_{0}}{L^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{L^{4}}{4}$.

steps.title: Centre of mass
steps.bodyLatex: $x_{cm} = \dfrac{L^{4}/4}{L^{3}/3} = \dfrac{3L}{4}$ from the $x = 0$ end (the mass is concentrated towards the dense end).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) $\dfrac{3L}{4}$.

verification.note: SymPy: integrate(x*x^2,(x,0,L))/integrate(x^2,(x,0,L)) = 3L/4.

jelet-2025-q054.conceptSummary: A rolling disc has translational plus rotational kinetic energy $\tfrac{1}{2}MV^{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}I\omega^{2} = \tfrac{3}{4}MV^{2}$; all of it becomes $Mgh$.

steps.title: Kinetic energy of rolling
steps.bodyLatex: For a disc $I = \tfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}$ and rolling without slipping gives $\omega = V/R$: $KE = \tfrac{1}{2}MV^{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}\cdot\dfrac{V^{2}}{R^{2}} = \tfrac{3}{4}MV^{2}$.

steps.title: Energy conservation
steps.bodyLatex: Static friction in pure rolling does no work, so at the highest point (disc momentarily at rest) $Mgh = \tfrac{3}{4}MV^{2}$.

steps.title: Height
steps.bodyLatex: $h = \dfrac{3V^{2}}{4g}$ (independent of $M$, $R$ and the shape of the incline).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: (D) $\dfrac{V^{2}}{2g}$ would ignore rotation. Answer: (B) $\dfrac{3V^{2}}{4g}$.

jelet-2025-q055.conceptSummary: $Y = \dfrac{F/A}{\Delta l/l}$, so for identical wires $Y \propto \dfrac{\text{load}}{\text{extension}}$ = the reciprocal of the slope of the extension–load graph.

steps.title: Relation between slope and $Y$
steps.bodyLatex: $\Delta l = \dfrac{l}{AY}F$, so the slope of the extension (vertical) versus load (horizontal) line is $\dfrac{l}{AY}$. With the same $l$ and $A$, a steeper line means a smaller $Y$.

steps.title: Read the graph
steps.bodyLatex: Line B is steeper than line A (B stretches more for the same load).

steps.title: Compare
steps.bodyLatex: $\text{slope}_{B} > \text{slope}_{A} \Rightarrow Y_{B} < Y_{A}$, i.e. $Y_{A} > Y_{B}$. (C) and (D) are excluded: the slopes are unequal, and (D) would need B to be the stiffer wire.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) $Y_{A} > Y_{B}$.

verification.note: Verifier reads the two lines of fig-2025-q55.svg: slope_B/slope_A = Y_A/Y_B > 1, so only option A holds.

jelet-2025-q056.conceptSummary: Floating equilibrium: weight of the cylinder = total buoyant force from the two liquids it displaces.

steps.title: Weight
steps.bodyLatex: With cross-section $A$: $W = dALg$.

steps.title: Buoyant force
steps.bodyLatex: Length $pL$ is in the denser liquid ($n\rho$) and $(1 - p)L$ in the lighter one ($\rho$): $F_{B} = n\rho\,A(pL)g + \rho\,A(1 - p)Lg$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) $\{1 + (n - 1)p\}\rho$.

verification.note: SymPy: solve(d A L g - (n rho A p L g + rho A (1-p) L g), d) = rho (1 + (n-1) p).

jelet-2025-q057.conceptSummary: Internal energy is a state function: $\Delta U_{a\to b}$ found from path $acb$ also holds for path $adb$.

steps.title: Path $acb$
steps.bodyLatex: First law: $\Delta U = Q - W = 200 - 80 = 120$ J.

steps.title: Path $adb$
steps.bodyLatex: Same end states, so $\Delta U = 120$ J; with $Q = 144$ J, $W = Q - \Delta U = 144 - 120 = 24$ J.

steps.title: Consistency with the figure
steps.bodyLatex: $adb$ runs along the lower pressure (isobar $ad$, then isochor $db$), so it does less work than $acb$ ($24 < 80$ J), as expected.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) $24$ J.

jelet-2025-q058.conceptSummary: Isothermal expansion is a falling rectangular hyperbola $PV = $ const; the return at constant pressure is a horizontal line at the lower pressure.

steps.title: First process (A to intermediate state)
steps.bodyLatex: Isothermal: $PV = nRT$ constant. As $V$ goes $V \to 3V$, $P$ falls from $P_{A}$ to $P_{A}/3$ along a convex decreasing curve (a hyperbola), not a straight line.

steps.title: Second process (to B)
steps.bodyLatex: Compression $3V \to V$ at constant pressure $P_{A}/3$: a horizontal line traversed right to left, ending at B with $V_{B} = V$, $P_{B} = P_{A}/3 < P_{A}$ (B lies below A).

steps.title: Check the graphs
steps.bodyLatex: (A) draws the isothermal as a straight line. (C) does the processes in the wrong order (isobaric expansion first, from A at the lower pressure). (D) returns along a sloping line, so the pressure is not constant. (B) shows the falling curve from A at $V$ to $3V$ and then the horizontal line back to B at $V$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B).

verification.note: Verifier parses each option SVG: only (B) has a convex decreasing first leg from A (V to 3V) followed by a horizontal leg back to B at V, with arrowheads along the drawing direction.

jelet-2025-q059.conceptSummary: In SHM $\nu^{2} = \omega^{2}(a^{2} - x^{2})$; subtract the two instances to eliminate the amplitude $a$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: (C) inverts the ratio: $\dfrac{\nu_{1}^{2} - \nu_{2}^{2}}{x_{1}^{2} - x_{2}^{2}} = -\omega^{2}$, so it would be $2\pi\sqrt{-\omega^{2}}$, not even real (and has the wrong dimensions). (B) and (D) add the squares instead of subtracting them, which does not eliminate $a$. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: with v_i^2 = w^2 (a^2 - x_i^2), option A simplifies to 2 pi / w; B, C, D do not.

jelet-2025-q060.conceptSummary: The two lenses are in contact: $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{f_{2}}$ with the lens-maker's formula for each, sharing the curved surface of radius R.

steps.title: Plano-convex lens ($\mu_{1}$)
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{1}{f_{1}} = (\mu_{1} - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = \dfrac{\mu_{1} - 1}{R}$.

steps.title: Plano-concave lens ($\mu_{2}$)
steps.bodyLatex: Its curved surface has the same radius but is concave: $\dfrac{1}{f_{2}} = -\dfrac{\mu_{2} - 1}{R}$.

steps.title: Combine
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{\mu_{1} - 1}{R} - \dfrac{\mu_{2} - 1}{R} = \dfrac{\mu_{1} - \mu_{2}}{R} \Rightarrow F = \dfrac{R}{\mu_{1} - \mu_{2}}$. (If $\mu_{1} = \mu_{2}$ the combination is a parallel glass slab, $F \to \infty$, as expected.)

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) $\dfrac{R}{\mu_{1} - \mu_{2}}$.

verification.note: SymPy: 1/((mu1-1)/R - (mu2-1)/R) simplifies to R/(mu1 - mu2).

jelet-2025-q061.conceptSummary: Heat lost = heat gained for each mixture gives the ratios of the specific heats; then apply the same balance to A + C.

steps.title: A and B mixed at $13^{\circ}$C
steps.bodyLatex: $mc_{A}(13 - 10) = mc_{B}(15 - 13) \Rightarrow 3c_{A} = 2c_{B} \Rightarrow c_{A} = \tfrac{2}{3}c_{B}$.

steps.title: B and C mixed at $16^{\circ}$C
steps.bodyLatex: $mc_{B}(16 - 15) = mc_{C}(20 - 16) \Rightarrow c_{B} = 4c_{C} \Rightarrow c_{C} = \tfrac{1}{4}c_{B}$.

steps.title: A and C mixed at $\theta$
steps.bodyLatex: $mc_{A}(\theta - 10) = mc_{C}(20 - \theta) \Rightarrow \tfrac{2}{3}(\theta - 10) = \tfrac{1}{4}(20 - \theta) \Rightarrow 8\theta - 80 = 60 - 3\theta \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{140}{11}\,^{\circ}\text{C} \approx 12.7^{\circ}\text{C}$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: The result lies between $10^{\circ}$C and $20^{\circ}$C, nearer A (larger heat capacity), so (C) and (D) are impossible and (B) $\approx 7.9^{\circ}$C is below both. Answer: (A) $\dfrac{140}{11}\,^{\circ}$C.

verification.note: SymPy: c_A = 2/3 c_B, c_C = c_B/4; solve(c_A(th-10) - c_C(20-th)) = 140/11.

jelet-2025-q062.conceptSummary: With heat supplied at a constant rate, $dQ = mc\,dT$ on a sloping part, so the slope of the temperature–heat graph is $\dfrac{dT}{dQ} = \dfrac{1}{mc}$.

steps.title: Identify the phases
steps.bodyLatex: OA: solid heating; AB (flat): melting; BC: liquid heating; CD (flat): boiling; DE: heating of the vapour.

steps.title: Slope of a rising segment
steps.bodyLatex: On a sloping part no phase change occurs: $Q = mc\,\Delta T \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta T}{\Delta Q} = \dfrac{1}{mc}$, the inverse of the heat capacity of the phase present.

steps.title: Apply to DE
steps.bodyLatex: DE follows the boiling plateau, so the material is vapour: slope of DE $= \dfrac{1}{(mc)_{\text{vapour}}}$. Latent heats correspond to the lengths of the flat parts, not to slopes.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) Inverse of heat capacity of vapour.

verification.note: SymPy: T(Q) = T_D + (Q - Q_D)/(m c_v) gives dT/dQ = 1/(m c_v); the verifier confirms AB and CD are flat and DE rises in fig-2025-q62.svg.

jelet-2025-q063.conceptSummary: Steady conduction: $H = \dfrac{kA\Delta T}{l} \propto \dfrac{r^{2}}{l}$ for the same material and temperature difference.

steps.title: Heat current
steps.bodyLatex: $H = \dfrac{k\pi r^{2}\Delta T}{l}$.

steps.title: Ratio
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{H_{1}}{H_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}\right)^{2}\dfrac{l_{2}}{l_{1}} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{2}\cdot\dfrac{2}{1} = \dfrac{8}{9}$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $8 : 9$.

jelet-2025-q064.conceptSummary: Einstein's equation $\tfrac{1}{2}mV_{\max}^{2} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi$ with the same work function $\phi$ for both blocks.

steps.title: Same metal, same work function
steps.bodyLatex: Both blocks are of the same metal, so $\phi$ is identical; the stem states photo-electrons are emitted from both, so $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{2}} > \phi$ as well.

steps.title: Photon energies
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} = \dfrac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{350\text{ nm}} \approx 3.54$ eV and $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{2}} = \dfrac{1240}{540} \approx 2.30$ eV.

steps.title: Compare maximum speeds
steps.bodyLatex: $\tfrac{1}{2}mV_{1}^{2} - \tfrac{1}{2}mV_{2}^{2} = hc\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_{2}}\right) \approx 1.25\text{ eV} > 0$, independent of $\phi$. Hence $V_{1} > V_{2}$; the size of the blocks is irrelevant, so (D) is wrong.

verification.note: SymPy: KE1 - KE2 = h c (1/350nm - 1/540nm) = 1.25 eV > 0 for any common work function.

jelet-2025-q065.conceptSummary: The ball's speed is unchanged in water only if it enters at the terminal velocity; equate $\sqrt{2gh}$ to Stokes' terminal velocity.

steps.title: Speed after free fall
steps.bodyLatex: $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.

steps.title: Equate
steps.bodyLatex: $2gh = v_{t}^{2} \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{400}{2 \times 9.8} = 20.41$ m.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) $20{\cdot}41$ m.

verification.note: SymPy/numeric: v_t = 2 r^2 (rho - sigma) g / (9 eta) = 20 m/s; h = v_t^2/(2g) = 20.408 m.

jelet-2025-q066.conceptSummary: Uniform acceleration from rest gives $x = \tfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$ (an upward-opening parabola starting with zero slope); afterwards $x$ grows linearly with the slope equal to the velocity at $t = 4$ s.

steps.title: First 4 s
steps.bodyLatex: $x = \tfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$: $x(0) = 0$, slope $v(0) = 0$, curve concave up.

steps.title: After 4 s
steps.bodyLatex: $v = 4a$ constant, so $x = 8a + 4a(t - 4)$: a straight line. Velocity is continuous, so the line is tangent to the parabola at $t = 4$ (no kink).

steps.title: Evaluate every graph
steps.bodyLatex: (A) concave down at the start (decelerating) and then $x$ decreases — FALSE. (B) concave down, then a sudden jump in slope — FALSE. (C) correct parabola, but $x$ becomes constant (car stops) — FALSE. (D) concave-up curve from the origin followed by a straight line continuing its slope — TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D).

verification.note: Verifier reads each option SVG: only (D) fits x = a t^2 (a > 0, zero initial slope) on [0, 4] followed by a line of slope 2 a t_4 (C^1 join).

jelet-2025-q067.conceptSummary: For a light string over a smooth light pulley the tension equals the applied pull $F$; then use Newton's law and work–energy for the block.

steps.title: Tension
steps.bodyLatex: The string is light and the pulley smooth and light, so the tension is the same throughout and equals the pull: $T = F = 40$ N. (A) is FALSE.

steps.title: Acceleration and displacement
steps.bodyLatex: For the block: $T - mg = ma \Rightarrow 40 - 20 = 2a \Rightarrow a = 10$ m/s$^{2}$ upward. In $t = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{10}}$ s from rest: $s = \tfrac{1}{2}at^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2}(10)\dfrac{4}{10} = 2$ m upward. (D) is TRUE.

steps.title: Work done
steps.bodyLatex: By tension on the block: $W_{T} = Ts = 40 \times 2 = 80$ J — (C) TRUE. By gravity: $W_{g} = -mgs = -20 \times 2 = -40$ J, not $-20$ J — (B) FALSE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C), (D).

jelet-2025-q068.conceptSummary: Gravity is a central, conservative force: angular momentum about the Sun and total mechanical energy are conserved; KE and PE vary with distance.

steps.title: Angular momentum
steps.bodyLatex: The force on the planet points towards the Sun, so its torque about the Sun is zero: $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times m\vec{v}$ is constant (Kepler's second law). (B) TRUE.

steps.title: Total energy
steps.bodyLatex: Gravity is conservative and there is no other force: $E = K + U = -\dfrac{GMm}{2a}$ is constant. (D) TRUE.

steps.title: Kinetic and potential energy
steps.bodyLatex: $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}$ changes as $r$ varies between perihelion and aphelion; $K = E - U$ therefore changes too (the planet is fastest at perihelion). (A) and (C) FALSE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B), (D).

verification.note: SymPy/numeric: Kepler orbit with e = 0.3: L = m sqrt(G M a (1-e^2)) and E constant; U and K differ between perihelion and aphelion.

jelet-2025-q069.conceptSummary: Compare the heat needed to melt all the ice and warm it to $100^{\circ}$C with the heat available from condensing all the steam.

steps.title: Heat to take the ice to water at $100^{\circ}$C
Heat available from the steam
steps.bodyLatex: Condensing all the steam would release $5000 \times 540 = 2.7 \times 10^{6}$ cal $> Q_{\text{need}}$, so not all steam condenses and the mixture stays at $100^{\circ}$C. (B) TRUE, (A) impossible (FALSE).

steps.title: Final composition
steps.bodyLatex: Water $= 10 + 3\tfrac{1}{3} = 13\tfrac{1}{3}$ kg — (C) TRUE. Steam left $= 5 - 3\tfrac{1}{3} = 1\tfrac{2}{3}$ kg — (D) TRUE. (Total $15$ kg conserved.)

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B), (C), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: Q_need = 1.8e6 cal < 2.7e6 cal; condensed 10000/3 g; water 40/3 kg, steam 5/3 kg, T = 100 C.

jelet-2025-q070.conceptSummary: Expand $(\vec{A}\times\vec{B})\times(\vec{C}\times\vec{D})$ two ways with the vector triple product.

steps.title: Expansion 1
steps.bodyLatex: $\overline{P} = [(\overline{A}\times\overline{B})\cdot\overline{D}]\,\overline{C} - [(\overline{A}\times\overline{B})\cdot\overline{C}]\,\overline{D}$: a combination of $\overline{C}$ and $\overline{D}$, so $\overline{P}$ lies in the plane of $\overline{C}$ and $\overline{D}$. (C) TRUE.

steps.title: Expansion 2
steps.bodyLatex: $\overline{P} = -(\overline{C}\times\overline{D})\times(\overline{A}\times\overline{B}) = [(\overline{C}\times\overline{D})\cdot\overline{A}]\,\overline{B} - [(\overline{C}\times\overline{D})\cdot\overline{B}]\,\overline{A}$: so $\overline{P}$ lies in the plane of $\overline{A}$ and $\overline{B}$. (B) TRUE.

steps.title: Line of intersection
steps.bodyLatex: Lying in both planes, $\overline{P}$ is parallel to their line of intersection (equivalently $\overline{P} \perp \overline{A}\times\overline{B}$ and $\overline{P} \perp \overline{C}\times\overline{D}$, the two plane normals). (D) TRUE.

steps.title: (A)
steps.bodyLatex: $\overline{P}$ lies in the plane of $\overline{A}, \overline{B}$, so it cannot be perpendicular to that plane (unless $\overline{P} = \vec{0}$). (A) FALSE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B), (C), (D).

verification.note: SymPy: for generic symbolic A, B, C, D, P.(A x B) = P.(C x D) = 0 and P equals both triple-product expansions; P is not parallel to A x B.

jelet-2025-q071.conceptSummary: The azimuthal quantum number $l = 0, 1, 2, 3$ corresponds to $s, p, d, f$.

steps.title: Decode $l$
steps.bodyLatex: $l = 3$ is an $f$ orbital (allowed since $l \leq n - 1 = 4$).

steps.title: Designation
steps.bodyLatex: $n = 5$, $l = 3$ gives the $5f$ orbital.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) $5f$.

verification.note: Check: 'spdfg'[3] = 'f' and 3 <= 5 - 1.

jelet-2025-q072.conceptSummary: PCl$_{5}$ is trigonal bipyramidal ($sp^{3}d$): three equatorial and two axial P–Cl bonds of different lengths.

steps.title: Geometry
steps.bodyLatex: P has $5$ bond pairs and no lone pair: VSEPR gives a trigonal bipyramid ($sp^{3}d$ hybridisation).

steps.title: Bond types
steps.bodyLatex: The $3$ equatorial bonds (at $120^{\circ}$, about $202$ pm) are equivalent; the $2$ axial bonds (at $90^{\circ}$ to the equatorial plane, about $240$ pm) are longer because they suffer more bond-pair repulsion.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Two types of P–Cl bonds. Answer: (B) Two.

verification.note: Geometry check: in an ideal trigonal bipyramid the axial (3 neighbours at 90 deg) and equatorial (2 at 90 deg, 2 at 120 deg) environments differ -> 2 distinct bond classes.

jelet-2025-q073.conceptSummary: Doping Si (group 14) with a group-15 donor adds a free electron per impurity atom: negative charge carriers, i.e. an $n$-type semiconductor.

steps.title: Electron-rich impurity
steps.bodyLatex: An electron-rich dopant such as P or As has $5$ valence electrons; $4$ form bonds with neighbouring Si atoms and the $5$th is loosely bound.

steps.title: Charge carriers
steps.bodyLatex: These extra electrons are the majority carriers (negative), so conduction increases and the material is $n$-type. Electron-deficient dopants (B, Al) would give $p$-type.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) $n$-type semiconductor.

verification.note: Valence count: dopant group 15 (5 e-) in a group-14 lattice leaves 5 - 4 = +1 free electron -> n-type.

jelet-2025-q074.conceptSummary: Track oxidation numbers of N: $+2$ (NO) and $+4$ (N$_{2}$O$_{4}$) both go to $+3$ (NO$_{2}^{-}$).

steps.title: Balanced equation
steps.bodyLatex: $2\text{NO} + \text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4} + 4\text{OH}^{-} \rightarrow 4\text{NO}_{2}^{-} + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ (atoms and charge balance; electrons lost $2 \times 1$ = electrons gained $2 \times 1$).

steps.title: Classify
steps.bodyLatex: Two species of the same element in different oxidation states give a single intermediate oxidation state: this is comproportionation (the reverse of disproportionation).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) Comproportionation.

verification.note: SymPy: oxidation numbers +2, +4 -> +3; element and charge balance of 2NO + N2O4 + 4OH- -> 4NO2- + 2H2O verified.

steps.title: Evaluate each statement
steps.bodyLatex: (A) Y at pH $7$ is neutral, not acidic — FALSE. (B) $\dfrac{10^{-6}}{10^{-7}} = 10$: X is $10$ times more acidic — TRUE. (C) In Y, $[\text{OH}^{-}] = K_{w}/[\text{H}^{+}] = 10^{-7} = [\text{H}^{+}]$, so $[\text{OH}^{-}] > [\text{H}^{+}]$ is FALSE. (D) FALSE since (B) is correct.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) Solution X is 10 times more acidic than solution Y.

verification.note: SymPy: 10^-6 / 10^-7 = 10; Kw/10^-7 = 10^-7 = [H+] in Y, so OH- is not greater.

steps.title: Reaction quotient
steps.bodyLatex: For Zn + Cu$^{2+}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ Cu + Zn$^{2+}$ ($n = 2$), solids have unit activity: $Q = \dfrac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} = \dfrac{0.1}{0.1} = 1$.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.bodyLatex: Only the ratio of the two ion concentrations matters; equal concentrations leave the EMF at its standard value. Negative values (C), (D) would mean the reaction is non-spontaneous, which is not the case.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) 1.10 V.

jelet-2025-q077.conceptSummary: Le Chatelier: decreasing the volume (raising the pressure) shifts an equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas.

steps.title: Count gaseous moles, $\Delta n_{g} = n_{g}(\text{products}) - n_{g}(\text{reactants})$
Effect of compression
steps.bodyLatex: Compression favours the direction that reduces $n_{g}$. Only (C), with $\Delta n_{g} < 0$, shifts forward. (A) is unaffected; (B) and (D) shift backwards, towards reactants.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) H$_{2}$O($l$) + CO$_{2}$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_{2}$CO$_{3}$(aq.).

verification.note: Parsed from the option text: Delta n_gas = 0, +1, -1, +1; only C is negative.

jelet-2025-q078.conceptSummary: A salt of a strong base and a weak acid hydrolyses to give a basic solution; salts of a strong acid with a strong base are neutral.

steps.title: Classify the salts
steps.bodyLatex: KCl and NaCl come from a strong acid and a strong base, so they are neutral (pH 7). CuSO$_{4}$ comes from a weak base and a strong acid: hydrated Cu$^{2+}$ hydrolyses and the solution is acidic (pH below 7). Na$_{2}$CO$_{3}$ comes from a strong base and the weak acid H$_{2}$CO$_{3}$.

steps.title: Hydrolysis of carbonate
steps.bodyLatex: CO$_{3}^{2-}$ + H$_{2}$O $\rightleftharpoons$ HCO$_{3}^{-}$ + OH$^{-}$, $K_{b} = \dfrac{K_{w}}{K_{a2}} = \dfrac{10^{-14}}{4.7 \times 10^{-11}} \approx 2.1 \times 10^{-4}$. For 0.1 M, $[\text{OH}^{-}] \approx \sqrt{K_{b}C} \approx 4.6 \times 10^{-3}$ M, so pH $\approx 11.7$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Na$_{2}$CO$_{3}$ gives the highest pH. Answer: (C).

verification.note: Numeric: pH(0.1 M) = 7, 7, 11.66, ~4.5 for KCl, NaCl, Na2CO3, CuSO4.

jelet-2025-q079.conceptSummary: In the electrolysis of an aqueous salt, the cathode reduces whichever species has the higher reduction potential. For Na, Mg, Ca and Al this is water, so H$_{2}$ is evolved instead of the metal.

steps.title: Which is reduced?
steps.bodyLatex: Every metal ion has a potential far below that of water, so water is reduced first in each case: H$_{2}$ forms at the cathode and the metal is never deposited. Industrially all four are made by electrolysing fused salts instead: the Downs cell for NaCl, fused MgCl$_{2}$, fused CaCl$_{2}$, and Al$_{2}$O$_{3}$ in molten cryolite (Hall–Héroult).

steps.title: Why the item was withdrawn
steps.bodyLatex: None of (A)–(D) can be obtained by electrolysing an aqueous solution of its salts, so the single-correct question has no correct option. (Metals such as Cu, Ag or Zn, with potentials above or near that of water, would have worked.) WBJEEB's final answer key marks Q79 W (withdrawn).

steps.title: Marking
steps.bodyLatex: Q79 is a Category-I item marked W (withdrawn). It awards the full $+1$ mark ($+12$ twelfths) to every candidate, whatever they marked.

verification.note: Numeric: E(M^n+/M) = -2.71, -2.37, -2.87, -1.66 V, all below E(H2O/H2) = -0.83 V; no option correct -> W, +1 mark (+12 twelfths) to all.

jelet-2025-q080.conceptSummary: Track the oxidation number of nitrogen: $0$ in N$_{2}$, $-3$ in NH$_{3}$.

steps.title: Electrons per N$_{2}$
steps.bodyLatex: Each N gains $3$ electrons. The N$_{2}$ molecule in the conversion has two N atoms: $2 \times 3 = 6$ electrons. Balanced half-reaction: N$_{2}$ + 6H$^{+}$ + 6e$^{-}$ $\rightarrow$ 2NH$_{3}$ (charge: $+6 - 6 = 0$ on both sides).

steps.title: Note
steps.bodyLatex: $3$ (option B) is the count per N atom, i.e. per NH$_{3}$. The conversion as printed starts from one N$_{2}$ molecule, so $6$ electrons are involved.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) 6.

verification.note: SymPy: ox(N) 0 -> -3; 2 x 3 = 6 e- per N2; N2 + 6H+ + 6e- -> 2NH3 atom- and charge-balanced.

jelet-2025-q081.conceptSummary: Traditional IUPAC rules (1979/1993, used in the WBJEE/JELET syllabus): the principal chain must contain the maximum number of multiple bonds; then number it to give the multiple bonds the lowest locants.

steps.title: Choose the principal chain
steps.bodyLatex: The printed structure is CH$_{3}$–CH$_{2}$–C$\equiv$C–CH(–CH=CH$_{2}$)(–CH$_{2}$–CH(CH$_{3}$)$_{2}$). The chain CH$_{2}$=CH–CH–C$\equiv$C–CH$_{2}$–CH$_{3}$ (7 C) contains both the double and the triple bond. The longer 8-C chain through the isobutyl group contains only the triple bond, so the 7-C chain is principal: hept-en-yne.

steps.title: Numbering
steps.bodyLatex: From the vinyl end the multiple bonds sit at $\{1, 4\}$ (ene 1, yne 4). From the ethyl end they sit at $\{3, 6\}$. The lowest set $\{1, 4\}$ wins: hept-1-en-4-yne.

steps.title: Substituent
steps.bodyLatex: C-3 carries CH$_{2}$–CH(CH$_{3}$)$_{2}$. Numbered from its point of attachment, this is a propyl chain with a methyl group on its C-2: 2-methylpropyl (isobutyl).

steps.title: Name and the other options
steps.bodyLatex: 3-(2-Methylpropyl)hept-1-en-4-yne is option (A). (B) puts the triple bond at 5 instead of 3. (C) follows the 2013 recommendations, which rank chain length first (oct-3-yne with ethenyl at 5 and methyl at 7), but lists the prefixes out of alphabetical order. The correct 2013 name would be 5-ethenyl-7-methyloct-3-yne. Under the convention the paper follows, the key is (A).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) 3-(2-Methylpropyl) hept-1-en-4-yne.

verification.note: Graph namer run on the structure parsed from fig-2025-q81.svg (C11H18, valences checked): 1993 rules -> 3-(2-methylpropyl)hept-1-en-4-yne = A; 2013 rules -> 5-ethenyl-7-methyloct-3-yne (matches no option exactly).

jelet-2025-q082.conceptSummary: Same molecular formula with different functional groups = functional (functional-group) isomerism.

steps.title: Identify the compounds
steps.bodyLatex: Left: CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$COOH, propanoic acid (a carboxylic acid). Right: HCOOCH$_{2}$CH$_{3}$, ethyl methanoate (an ester).

steps.title: Molecular formulae
steps.bodyLatex: Both are C$_{3}$H$_{6}$O$_{2}$, so they are structural isomers.

steps.title: Type
steps.bodyLatex: The functional groups differ (–COOH against –COO–). Chain and positional isomers keep the same functional group, and geometrical isomerism is a kind of stereoisomerism, not structural isomerism. So this is functional isomerism.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) Functional Isomerism.

verification.note: Graph check: both C3H6O2; functional groups carboxylic acid vs ester -> functional isomers.

jelet-2025-q083.conceptSummary: A Grignard reagent is a very strong base: with a compound carrying an acidic O–H it is simply protonated to the alkane.

steps.title: Step (i)
steps.bodyLatex: CH$_{3}$Cl + Mg $\xrightarrow{\text{ether}}$ CH$_{3}$MgCl (methylmagnesium chloride).

steps.title: Step (ii)
steps.bodyLatex: CH$_{3}$COOH has an acidic O–H ($pK_{a} \approx 4.8$, against about $50$ for CH$_{4}$). The carbanion-like CH$_{3}^{\delta-}$ takes the proton far faster than it could add to the C=O: CH$_{3}$MgCl + CH$_{3}$COOH $\rightarrow$ CH$_{4}$ + CH$_{3}$COOMgCl.

steps.title: Other options
steps.bodyLatex: C$_{2}$H$_{6}$ would need Wurtz-type coupling. CH$_{3}$COOCH$_{3}$ would need esterification, which is not what a Grignard reagent does.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) CH$_{4}$.

verification.note: Atom balance: CH3MgCl + CH3COOH -> CH4 + CH3COOMgCl balanced (C3H7O2MgCl both sides); pKa 4.8 << 50.

jelet-2025-q084.conceptSummary: The hybridization of a carbanion carbon depends on the carbanion: steric number 4 gives $sp^{3}$, resonance or vinyl carbanions are $sp^{2}$, and acetylide is $sp$.

steps.title: Simple alkyl carbanion
steps.bodyLatex: CH$_{3}^{-}$: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair, steric number 4, so $sp^{3}$ (pyramidal, isoelectronic with NH$_{3}$). This is the usual textbook answer.

steps.title: Other carbanions
steps.bodyLatex: Allyl and benzyl carbanions put the lone pair in a $p$ orbital conjugated with the $\pi$ system, so the carbon is $sp^{2}$ (planar). A vinyl carbanion, CH$_{2}$=CH$^{-}$, is $sp^{2}$. Acetylide, HC$\equiv$C$^{-}$, has steric number 2, so it is $sp$. ($sp^{4}$ is not a hybridization.)

steps.title: Why the item was withdrawn
steps.bodyLatex: \"A carbanion\" does not name a specific species, so (A) $sp$, (B) $sp^{2}$ and (C) $sp^{3}$ are each correct for some carbanion. A single-correct Category-I question therefore has no unique answer, and WBJEEB's final answer key marks Q84 W (withdrawn). For a simple alkyl carbanion the answer would be $sp^{3}$.

steps.title: Marking
steps.bodyLatex: Q84 is a Category-I item marked W (withdrawn). It awards the full $+1$ mark ($+12$ twelfths) to every candidate, whatever they marked.

verification.note: Steric numbers: CH3- 4 (sp3), allyl/vinyl 3 (sp2), HC#C- 2 (sp) -> options A, B, C all realisable -> not single-correct -> W, +1 mark (+12 twelfths) to all.

jelet-2025-q085.conceptSummary: Terminal alkynes are acidic ($pK_{a} \approx 25$). NaNH$_{2}$ ($pK_{a}$(NH$_{3}$) $\approx 35$) forms the acetylide, which is alkylated by a primary halide in an S$_{N}$2 reaction. Both C–H bonds of ethyne are replaced in turn.

steps.title: First alkylation
steps.bodyLatex: HC$\equiv$CH + NaNH$_{2}$ $\rightarrow$ HC$\equiv$C$^{-}$Na$^{+}$ + NH$_{3}$. Then HC$\equiv$C$^{-}$ + CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$Br $\rightarrow$ HC$\equiv$C–CH$_{2}$CH$_{3}$ (but-1-yne) + Br$^{-}$.

steps.title: Second alkylation
steps.bodyLatex: But-1-yne is still a terminal alkyne. NaNH$_{2}$ deprotonates it again, and the excess ethyl bromide alkylates the new acetylide: CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$C$\equiv$C$^{-}$ + CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$Br $\rightarrow$ CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$–C$\equiv$C–CH$_{2}$CH$_{3}$ (hex-3-yne, C$_{6}$H$_{10}$). The scheme assumes enough NaNH$_{2}$ for both deprotonations, as usual when the halide is in excess.

steps.title: Reject the drawn structures
steps.bodyLatex: (A) is (E)-hex-3-ene, C$_{6}$H$_{12}$; reaching it would need a further reduction such as Na/liq. NH$_{3}$, which is not a step here. (C) and (D) put NH$_{2}$ (and Br) on vinylic carbons. S$_{N}$2 alkylation of an acetylide cannot do that, and amide is used only as a base.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$—C$\equiv$C—CH$_{2}$CH$_{3}$.

verification.note: Stoichiometric simulation: HC#CH -> (deprotonate, SN2 EtBr) x2 -> Et-C#C-Et, C6H10, an alkyne; option formulas C6H12 / C6H10 / C4H9N / C2H4BrN -> only B.

jelet-2025-q086.conceptSummary: An $\alpha$-particle is repelled by the gold nucleus through the inverse-square Coulomb force. It never comes close enough for the short-range nuclear force to act. A repulsive inverse-square orbit with positive energy is a hyperbola.

steps.title: Statement I — Coulomb force
steps.bodyLatex: Both $\alpha$ ($+2e$) and the Au nucleus ($+79e$) are positive, so the scattering is caused by Coulomb repulsion $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}}\dfrac{(2e)(79e)}{r^{2}}$. TRUE.

steps.title: Statement II — nuclear force
steps.bodyLatex: Closest approach for a 5.5 MeV $\alpha$: $d = \dfrac{1.44\text{ MeV fm} \times 158}{5.5\text{ MeV}} \approx 41$ fm. The Au nuclear radius is $1.2 \times 197^{1/3} \approx 7$ fm, and the nuclear force has a range of only a few fm, so it plays no part. FALSE.

steps.title: Statements III and IV — shape of the path
steps.bodyLatex: For a $1/r^{2}$ force the orbit is a conic with eccentricity $e = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{2EL^{2}}{mk^{2}}}$. The $\alpha$-particle is unbound ($E > 0$), so $e > 1$: the path is a hyperbola with the nucleus at the outer focus. A parabola needs $E = 0$ exactly. III FALSE, IV TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) I and (D) IV.

verification.note: Numeric: d_min = 41.4 fm >> R_Au = 7.0 fm; SymPy: e = sqrt(1 + 2 E L^2/(m k^2)) > 1 for E > 0. True set {A, D}.

jelet-2025-q087.conceptSummary: Dilution keeps the amount of solute fixed while the volume grows. Concentration falls, and by Ostwald's dilution law the degree of ionization rises.

steps.title: Concentration
steps.bodyLatex: $C_{1}V_{1} = C_{2}V_{2}$ with $V_{2} > V_{1}$ gives $C_{2} < C_{1}$: the concentration decreases. (IV) TRUE; (I) and (II) FALSE.

steps.title: Ionization
steps.bodyLatex: For an electrolyte AB $\rightleftharpoons$ A$^{+}$ + B$^{-}$, Ostwald's law gives $\alpha \approx \sqrt{K/C}$, so $\dfrac{d\alpha}{dC} < 0$: dilution increases the degree of ionization. A strong electrolyte is already almost fully ionized, hence \"may increase\". (III) TRUE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (C) III and (D) IV.

verification.note: SymPy: C2 = C1 V1/V2 < C1 for V2 > V1; d/dC sqrt(K/C) < 0. True set {C, D}.

jelet-2025-q088.conceptSummary: HBr adds through a carbocation (Markovnikov). The secondary cation next to a quaternary carbon undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to a more stable tertiary cation, so a rearranged and an unrearranged bromide are both formed.

steps.title: Protonation
steps.bodyLatex: H$^{+}$ adds to the terminal CH$_{2}$ (Markovnikov), giving the secondary cation (CH$_{3}$)$_{3}$C–C$^{+}$H–CH$_{3}$. Protonating C-2 would give a primary cation, which is not formed.

steps.title: Unrearranged product
steps.bodyLatex: Br$^{-}$ captures the secondary cation: (CH$_{3}$)$_{3}$C–CHBr–CH$_{3}$, 3-bromo-2,2-dimethylbutane = structure (I).

steps.title: 1,2-methyl shift
steps.bodyLatex: A methyl group migrates from the quaternary carbon to C$^{+}$, giving the tertiary cation (CH$_{3}$)$_{2}$C$^{+}$–CH(CH$_{3}$)$_{2}$. Br$^{-}$ capture gives 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane = structure (II), the major product.

steps.title: Evaluate every option
steps.bodyLatex: (A) I is formed — TRUE. (B) II is formed (major) — TRUE. (C) \"I and II\" — TRUE, since both are formed. (D) III (1-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane) would be the anti-Markovnikov (peroxide) product. IV (1-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane) would need a rearrangement followed by anti-Markovnikov addition. Neither forms with HBr alone — FALSE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A), (B), (C).

verification.note: Carbocation engine on the reactant graph parsed from fig-2025-q88.svg: Markovnikov 2° cation -> I; 1,2-CH3 shift to 3° -> II; III, IV not produced; graph isomorphism vs drawn I–IV. True set {A, B, C}.

jelet-2025-q089.conceptSummary: $K_{p} = K_{c}(RT)^{\Delta n_{g}}$. With $R = 0.0821$ L atm mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, $RT > 1$ at any ordinary temperature, so $K_{p} < K_{c}$ exactly when $\Delta n_{g} < 0$.

steps.title: Gaseous mole change
steps.bodyLatex: (I) N$_{2}$O$_{4}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NO$_{2}$: $\Delta n_{g} = +1$. (II) N$_{2}$ + 3H$_{2}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NH$_{3}$: $\Delta n_{g} = 2 - 4 = -2$. (III) H$_{2}$ + I$_{2}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2HI: $0$. (IV) CO + H$_{2}$O $\rightleftharpoons$ CO$_{2}$ + H$_{2}$: $0$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Only reaction II has $K_{p} < K_{c}$. Answer: (B) II.

verification.note: Parsed Delta n_g = +1, -2, 0, 0; (RT)^Delta n at 298 K: 24.5, 1.67e-3, 1, 1 -> only II < 1. True set {B}.
