jelet-2025-q090.conceptSummary: HNO$_{3}$ is a liquid oxoacid in which N is in its highest oxidation state, $+5$.

steps.title: Physical state
steps.bodyLatex: Pure HNO$_{3}$ melts at $-42^{\circ}$C and boils at $83^{\circ}$C, so it is a (fuming) liquid at room temperature. (A) FALSE.

steps.title: Oxoacid
steps.bodyLatex: Its structure is H–O–NO$_{2}$, with an ionisable H on oxygen bonded to N. It is an oxoacid of nitrogen. (B) TRUE.

steps.title: Redox behaviour
steps.bodyLatex: $+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +5$, the maximum for group 15. N cannot be oxidised further, so HNO$_{3}$ is not a reducing agent (C FALSE). It is readily reduced (to NO$_{2}$, NO, NH$_{4}^{+}$, …), so it is a strong oxidizing agent (D TRUE).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B), (D).

verification.note: Checks: mp 231 K < 298 K (liquid); ox(N) = +5 = group-15 maximum -> oxidant only. True set {B, D}.

jelet-2025-q091.conceptSummary: A PMMC instrument responds to the average (dc) value of the current, because its deflecting torque is proportional to $i$.

steps.title: Average over one period
steps.bodyLatex: $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{100\pi} = 0.02$ s. $I_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{1}{T}\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T}(5 + 5\sin 100\pi t)\,dt = 5 + 0 = 5$ A.

steps.title: Other options
steps.bodyLatex: $\left(5 + \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ A adds the dc value to the rms value of the ac part. That is not a meter reading: a moving-iron meter would read the rms value, $\sqrt{25 + 12.5} \approx 6.12$ A. 0 A would be the reading for the pure ac part alone.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) 5 A.

verification.note: SymPy: (1/T) integrate(5 + 5 sin(100 pi t), (t, 0, 1/50)) = 5.

jelet-2025-q092.conceptSummary: In an ideal transformer, input power equals output power. A resistive load has unity power factor.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) 0$\cdot$5A.

jelet-2025-q093.conceptSummary: A transformer is a static machine. With no rotating parts it has no friction or windage losses, so its efficiency is the highest of these machines.

steps.title: Losses
steps.bodyLatex: Rotating machines (dc shunt and series motors, induction motors) have copper and iron losses plus mechanical friction and windage losses. Brush and commutator losses add to these for dc machines, and the air gap raises the magnetising current of induction motors.

steps.title: Typical full-load efficiencies
steps.bodyLatex: Power transformers: 95–99%. DC shunt and series motors: roughly 75–90%. Single-phase induction motors: roughly 60–80%.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) Transformer.

verification.note: Data check: max of typical full-load efficiency ranges -> transformer (0.95-0.99).

steps.title: Set regulation to zero
steps.bodyLatex: $0 = \dfrac{V_{NL} - 10}{10} \times 100 \Rightarrow V_{NL} = 10$ V.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.bodyLatex: 0% regulation is an ideal supply: its output does not change between no load and full load. Option (D) would mean positive regulation, (C) negative regulation, and (B) is meaningless here.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) 10V.

verification.note: SymPy: solve((Vnl - 10)/10 = 0) -> Vnl = 10.

jelet-2025-q095.conceptSummary: Each branch current lags the common voltage by $\phi_{k} = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\omega L_{k}}{R_{k}}$. All three currents are in phase when the two branch angles are equal.

steps.title: Branch currents
steps.bodyLatex: The two R–L branches share the same voltage $V$: $I_{1} = \dfrac{V}{R_{1} + j\omega L_{1}}$, $I_{2} = \dfrac{V}{R_{2} + j\omega L_{2}}$, lagging by $\phi_{1} = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\omega L_{1}}{R_{1}}$ and $\phi_{2} = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\omega L_{2}}{R_{2}}$.

steps.title: Condition
steps.bodyLatex: $\phi_{1} = \phi_{2} \iff \dfrac{L_{1}}{R_{1}} = \dfrac{L_{2}}{R_{2}} \iff \dfrac{R_{1}}{R_{2}} = \dfrac{L_{1}}{L_{2}}$ (equal time constants). This is independent of $\omega$, so the 50 Hz value does not matter. Then $I = I_{1} + I_{2}$ is a sum of two phasors with the same angle, so it is in phase with both.

steps.title: Other options
steps.bodyLatex: $R_{1}R_{2} = L_{1}L_{2}$ (A) equates $\Omega^{2}$ with H$^{2}$, so it is not even dimensionally consistent. $R_{1}L_{1} = R_{2}L_{2}$ (C) is consistent but is not the equal-time-constant condition. Counter-example for both: $R_{1} = 1$, $L_{1} = 2$, $R_{2} = 2$, $L_{2} = 1$ satisfies (A) and (C) but gives $L_{1}/R_{1} = 2 \neq 0.5$.

verification.note: Netlist from fig-2025-q95.svg: two series R-L branches in parallel; SymPy phase test: B always in phase; A, C have counter-examples.

jelet-2025-q096.conceptSummary: Kirchhoff's current law for a transistor: $I_{E} = I_{B} + I_{C}$ (true for both PNP and NPN).

steps.title: Check
steps.bodyLatex: $\alpha = \dfrac{I_{C}}{I_{E}} = 0.99$ and $\beta = \dfrac{I_{C}}{I_{B}} = 99$, typical values. 10.1 mA (B) would wrongly add $I_{B}$ to $I_{E}$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) 9$\cdot$9 mA.

verification.note: SymPy: I_C = 10 - 1/10 = 99/10 mA; alpha = 0.99, beta = 99.

jelet-2025-q097.conceptSummary: CMOS (complementary MOS) pairs an n-channel pull-down network with a p-channel pull-up network.

steps.title: Structure
steps.bodyLatex: In a CMOS inverter the PMOS (source to $V_{DD}$) conducts when the input is 0 and the NMOS (source to ground) conducts when the input is 1. Both device types are used. (A) and (B) are FALSE.

steps.title: Static power
steps.bodyLatex: In either steady state one transistor is OFF, so there is no dc path from $V_{DD}$ to ground. Static current, and hence static power, is practically zero (only leakage). (C) FALSE.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (D) Employs both N-type and P-type MOSFETs.

verification.note: Switch model of the CMOS inverter: for input 0/1 exactly one device conducts -> no static VDD-GND path; needs both NMOS and PMOS.

jelet-2025-q098.conceptSummary: The phase of the closed-loop gain: non-inverting $1 + \dfrac{R_{f}}{R_{1}}$ is real and positive, so it gives $0^{\circ}$.

steps.title: Non-inverting gain from the virtual short
steps.bodyLatex: The input goes to the $+$ terminal and the feedback divider $R_{f}$, $R_{1}$ goes to the $-$ terminal. With an ideal op-amp, $v_{-} = v_{+} = v_{i}$ and no current enters the input, so $\dfrac{v_{o} - v_{i}}{R_{f}} = \dfrac{v_{i}}{R_{1}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{v_{o}}{v_{i}} = 1 + \dfrac{R_{f}}{R_{1}}$, which is real and positive.

steps.title: Gains with ideal op-amp
steps.bodyLatex: Inverting: $-\dfrac{R_{f}}{R_{1}}$, a $180^{\circ}$ shift. Non-inverting: $1 + \dfrac{R_{f}}{R_{1}} > 0$, a $0^{\circ}$ shift. Integrator: $-\dfrac{1}{j\omega RC} = \dfrac{j}{\omega RC}$, $+90^{\circ}$. Differentiator: $-j\omega RC$, $-90^{\circ}$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Only the non-inverting amplifier has no phase difference. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy: arg of gains at s = j w: pi, 0, pi/2, -pi/2 -> only B is 0.

jelet-2025-q099.conceptSummary: Distributive law $(A + B)(A + C) = A + BC$, then the complement law $A + A' = 1$.

steps.title: Check
steps.bodyLatex: The truth table of $(A + B)(A + B') + A'$ is 1 for all four input combinations.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) 1.

verification.note: Truth table over (A, B) in {0,1}^2: expression = 1 1 1 1 -> only option B.

jelet-2025-q100.conceptSummary: A NAND with both inputs tied together, fed with the same signal, acts as an inverter. Two NANDs of (A, B) followed by a NAND therefore give $\overline{\overline{AB}} = AB$.

steps.title: First stage
steps.bodyLatex: Both input NAND gates receive A and B: $G_{1} = G_{2} = \overline{AB}$.

steps.title: Output stage
steps.bodyLatex: $Y = \overline{G_{1}G_{2}} = \overline{\overline{AB}\cdot\overline{AB}} = \overline{\overline{AB}} = AB$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (B) AND Gate.

verification.note: Netlist extracted from fig-2025-q100.svg wire geometry (hop = no junction); truth table Y = 0001 = AND.
